charts.title: Food-system outcomes extend beyond crop yield
constraints: Keep production, nutrition, affordability, waste, ecosystems, and labor visible.
Do not relabel crop sensitivity as food security.

charts.title: Major-crop sensitivity uses two non-combinable study frames
constraints: Separate percent per decade from percent per degree Celsius.
Expose adaptation and carbon-dioxide-fertilization assumptions.

charts.title: A local groundwater planning case shows transition pressure
constraints: Hale County is a local planning estimate, not a national projection.
Do not interpret declining supply as an all-wells-fail date.

charts.title: National food-system evidence readiness is uneven
constraints: Readiness scores describe evidence coverage, not outcome quality.
Missing national baselines remain null.

charts.title: Proposed food-water-land model and release gates
constraints: This is a model contract, not a completed model.
Outputs stay unavailable until linked inputs and validation gates close.

charts.title: Four food-system strategies use the same decision dimensions
constraints: Options are not optimized portfolios.
Qualitative comparisons cannot establish national food-security outcomes.

charts.title: Basins connect food, water, energy, materials, people, and ecosystems
constraints: Basin conditions and governance remain geographically explicit.
Do not aggregate incompatible basin evidence into one national average.

charts.title: Essential outcomes and ecological constraints are joint gates
constraints: Engineering supply cannot override ecological, quality, rights, or affordability constraints.
Scores indicate decision requirements, not achieved outcomes.

charts.title: Portfolio contributions form a sequence, not an additive national total
constraints: Unavailable compatible contributions remain null.
Do not add case-study yields across regions or technologies.

charts.title: Essential-service portfolios face four planning conditions
constraints: Cells are response requirements, not outage probabilities.
Drought and infrastructure-failure effects require basin and utility models.

charts.title: Portfolio tradeoffs stay multi-dimensional
constraints: Do not collapse reliability, cost, energy, emissions, ecosystems, and equity into one score.
Unknown household and ecological burdens remain visible.

charts.title: Regional governance aligns authority with the physical system
constraints: The map is an implementation responsibility graph, not a jurisdictional completeness claim.
Tribal rights and local authority remain explicit.

charts.title: Versioned basin-food-industry model contract
constraints: No nationalized basin result is authorized.
Release requires water quantity, quality, return flow, food, industry, ecological, equity, and validation layers.
